advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm shutdown-held-back candidates cannot be clamped past the cursor by `reconcile_max_holdback_seconds`, or document/accept that an old gap patchset is dropped at shutdown just as it would be after repeated retryable failures.
evidence: reconcile.py:409-420 applies the ceiling uniformly: `ceiling = newest - max(0, cfg.reconcile_max_holdback_seconds)` then `if oldest < ceiling: _degraded('holdback_expired', ...)` and `target = min(newest, ceiling)`

The 9f63 regression test at tests/unit/test_review_bot.py deliberately keeps timestamps close: 'Timestamps sit close together so the hold-back stays well inside reconcile_max_holdback_seconds and the clamp ceiling is not what is under test.' — the drop-on-clamp shutdown case is untested.
advisory.finding: Candidates held back by the 9ec0 shutdown path are recorded in `held_back` with their event time and then run through the SAME `reconcile_max_holdback_seconds` ceiling clamp as retryable candidates. If the oldest shutdown-skipped candidate's event time is older than `newest - reconcile_max_holdback_seconds`, `_persist_cursor` emits `holdback_expired` and clamps `target` to the ceiling — advancing the cursor PAST that candidate and dropping it outside the next pass's `?t1=` window. That is exactly the silent-drop the change claims shutdown must never cause (9f63).
scenarios: A backfill pass over a large/old fetch window (newest far ahead of a stale gap patchset) receives a stop mid-pass; the skipped older candidate's event time is beyond the holdback ceiling and is clamped past, never re-admitted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm only one reconcile_loop/lifespan is ever live per process, or scope the stop signal per-loop/per-app rather than as a shared module global.
evidence: reconcile.py:_stop_requested is a bare module global; request_stop/clear_stop mutate it with `global _stop_requested`
app.py:119 `_reconcile.clear_stop()` at startup and app.py:159 `_reconcile.request_stop()` at shutdown both act on that single shared flag
The docstring acknowledges it is 'module state that outlives any one loop' but assumes only one lifespan is live at a time
advisory.finding: `_stop_requested` is process-global module state with no owner scoping, and `request_stop()` sets it unconditionally. In a process running two overlapping FastAPI app lifespans (or a test that starts a second app before the first's `clear_stop`), one app's shutdown flips the flag and causes the other app's freshly created reconciler to decline ALL candidates. The autouse test fixture and startup `clear_stop()` mitigate only the strictly-sequential case.
scenarios: Overlapping/concurrent lifespans in one interpreter (some test harnesses, graceful-restart with overlap); a second app's reconciler is born or forced into shutdown by the first app's request_stop().

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify `_event()` returns change id `rebar~main~Iabc`, or assert completion by count/suffix rather than a hard-coded id in test_shutdown_reconciler_drain_shares_the_queue_drain_budget.
evidence: The id is derived from the `_event()` helper, not asserted to equal Iabc anywhere the diff shows.
advisory.finding: In `test_shutdown_reconciler_drain_shares_the_queue_drain_budget` the webhook stub appends the change_id from the enqueued `_event()` to `started`/`completed`, but the assertion hard-codes `assert completed == ['rebar~main~Iabc']`. If `_event()`'s change id is not exactly `rebar~main~Iabc`, the test fails for the wrong reason (masking or misattributing the budget-sharing assertion it is meant to prove).
scenarios: `_event()` helper changes its default change id; the budget-sharing test breaks on an unrelated equality rather than the elapsed-time assertion.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that requests a stop, then enters a fresh `appmod.lifespan(...)` in the same process WITHOUT the autouse reset intervening, asserting the reconciler is active (not born shutting down) — pinning app.py's startup `clear_stop()`.
evidence: app.py diff adds: `# Re-arm the reconciler's cooperative-stop flag (module state, so a process that already ran a lifespan would otherwise start this one already shutting down). _reconcile.clear_stop()`
tests/unit/test_review_bot.py:982-984 autouse fixture `_reset_reconciler_stop_flag` calls `reconcile.clear_stop()` before AND after every test, pre-clearing the module flag
ABSENCE: grep for `clear_stop` in tests yields only the autouse reset (982/984) and the hold-back test's second-pass (1092); no test asserts a lifespan STARTUP re-arms a previously-requested stop

The stated purpose ('a process that already ran a lifespan would otherwise start this one already shutting down') describes exactly the scenario the autouse fixture erases, so the new line is untested and unfalsifiable by the suite
advisory.finding: The lifespan-startup re-arm (`_reconcile.clear_stop()` added in app.py) has no regression test: no test runs a second lifespan in the same process after a prior `request_stop()`, and the autouse `_reset_reconciler_stop_flag` fixture pre-clears the module flag before every test, so deleting the startup `clear_stop()` would not fail any test.
scenarios: A process reload / repeated lifespan in one interpreter where a prior shutdown left `_stop_requested = True` and startup fails to re-arm it — the reconciler would decline all work from birth
